query: How does HNSW achieve sub-millisecond search latency?
expected_answer: HNSW achieves sub-millisecond search by organizing vectors into hierarchical layers where upper layers skip large graph regions with greedy hill-climbing, narrowing down candidates before searching layer 0.

query: What is the formula and purpose of Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)?
expected_answer: RRF combines rankings from different retrieval models by summing 1 / (k + rank) across dense and sparse systems, setting k=60 as standard.

query: Why use BM25 alongside dense vector search?
expected_answer: BM25 catches exact keyword matches, domain codes, and proper nouns that semantic embeddings can miss, providing complementary sparse retrieval.

query: Explain the role of efSearch and how tuning it affects recall versus speed.
expected_answer: efSearch controls the size of the dynamic candidate list during query time; higher efSearch explores more neighbors improving recall at the cost of higher latency.
